story.headline: Nvidia Reportedly Preparing Investment in AI Inference Chip Maker d-Matrix
story.summary: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to invest in rival AI chip startup d-Matrix. The move underscores Nvidia's strategy to back emerging players in the artificial intelligence inference hardware sector.

draft.body:
Nvidia is preparing an investment in artificial intelligence chip startup d-Matrix, according to an October 8, 2026 report from [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/) citing three people with knowledge of the transaction. The planned Nvidia d-Matrix investment aims to make Nvidia's proprietary technologies compatible with rival semiconductor architectures, integrating third-party accelerators directly into the company's data center hardware ecosystem.

As reported by [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-plans-to-invest-in-ai-chip-rival-dmatrix-the-information-93CH-4940033), the financial terms of the transaction were not immediately disclosed.

## Strategic Motivations Behind the Nvidia d-Matrix Investment

According to [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-plans-to-invest-in-ai-chip-rival-dmatrix-the-information-93CH-4940033), d-Matrix develops server chips for artificial intelligence that compete directly against Nvidia hardware. Rather than treating such competitors solely as market rivals, Nvidia's planned funding is part of a corporate initiative to ensure interoperability between its established technology standards and alternative silicon architectures.

By bringing competing processor architectures into its hardware environment, Nvidia can maintain an architectural footprint in customer data centers that deploy specialized non-Nvidia accelerators for specific workloads.

[[FIG1]]

## Technical Interoperability via NVLink Fusion

The investment talks follow a significant technical milestone between the two companies reached in September 2026. One month prior to the investment reports, d-Matrix announced that it would adopt Nvidia's NVLink interconnect technology to link its Raptor processors with Nvidia systems in rack-scale data center environments, according to [DatacenterDynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/report-nvidia-plans-to-invest-in-inference-chip-startup-d-matrix/).

The integration relies on NVLink Fusion, an interconnect framework that Nvidia first unveiled in May 2025. NVLink Fusion is designed specifically to allow third-party chipmakers to develop semi-custom AI infrastructure by bridging non-Nvidia accelerator chips with Nvidia server architectures.

Through this standard, d-Matrix joins a roster of prominent semiconductor companies that have partnered with Nvidia around NVLink Fusion. According to [DatacenterDynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/report-nvidia-plans-to-invest-in-inference-chip-startup-d-matrix/), other announced partners for the interconnect platform include:
- Arm
- Fujitsu
- Intel
- MediaTek
- Qualcomm
- SiFive
- Synopsys

The adoption of NVLink Fusion by d-Matrix enables its Raptor processors to sit directly within Nvidia-based rack systems, facilitating unified data paths across heterogeneous computing platforms.

[[FIG2]]

## d-Matrix Hardware Architecture and Efficiency Claims

Founded in 2019 and based in Santa Clara, California, d-Matrix specializes in hardware tailored for AI inference tasks. According to [DatacenterDynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/report-nvidia-plans-to-invest-in-inference-chip-startup-d-matrix/), the startup designs accelerator cards created to make inferencing workloads faster and more efficient than traditional general-purpose configurations.

The company's commercial portfolio consists of a full-stack platform that includes Corsair inference accelerators, JetStream network interface cards (NICs), and the proprietary Aviator software stack.

When comparing its hardware to conventional GPU-based systems, d-Matrix claims significant operational advantages for AI inference workloads:
- 10X faster performance
- 3X lower total cost
- 3X to 5X improvement in energy efficiency

## Startup Valuation and Capitalization History

The discussions with Nvidia occur during an intensive period of growth and capital raising for the Santa Clara startup. As reported by [DatacenterDynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/report-nvidia-plans-to-invest-in-inference-chip-startup-d-matrix/), d-Matrix completed a $275 million Series C financing round in November 2025. That transaction valued the startup at $2 billion.

Fundraising efforts escalated in 2026. In July 2026, [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/) reported that d-Matrix was actively seeking additional equity financing, targeting an ambitious $5 billion valuation.
